title: Melchizedek, or the Secret Doctrine of the Bible
author: J. C. F. Grumbine
description: Melchizedek, or the Secret Doctrine of the Bible by J. C. F. (Jesse Charles Fremont) Grumbine, the American Spiritualist and occult teacher who headed the College of Psychical Sciences and Unfoldment and the Order of the White Rose (Boston: The Order of the White Rose, 1919). Taking as its motto Matthew 13:35, 'I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world', it argues that the Bible has been treated as a sealed book whose key was lost, and that its true value lies in an inner revelation hidden in symbol, allegory, parable and myth. In five lectures Grumbine asks who Melchizedek was, the mysterious priest-king 'without father, without mother' of Genesis and Hebrews, and describes his office and order; the secret doctrines of that order with their myths, mysteries, symbols, canons and philosophy; the secret doctrine on four planes of expression and manifestation; the Christ psychology and Christian mysticism; and the key and how it is applied to divine realisation and illumination. It is a characteristic text of American esoteric Christianity and of the Melchizedek priesthood motif.
